items.title: The metric pairing is an isomorphism to the dual, and the raised covector in an orthonormal frame
items.statement: Let (V,eta) be a 4-dimensional Lorentz vector space (def-lorentz-form-and-inertia): eta is symmetric and bilinear, nondegenerate in the sense that both radicals are {0} (def-matrix-radicals-rank-and-nondegeneracy-of-a-bilinear-form), and of inertia (3,1,0). Let V* be the algebraic dual (def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional). Then: (a) the map iota: V -> V*, iota(v)(w) := eta(v,w), is linear and injective, since iota(v) = 0 means eta(v,w) = 0 for all w in V, i.e. v lies in the left radical, which is {0}. (b) dim V* = dim V = 4, so iota is a linear bijection (rank-nullity, thm-rank-nullity). (c) Consequently for every covector k in V* there is a unique vector k^sharp in V with eta(k^sharp,w) = k(w) for all w in V; the assignment sharp: V* -> V, k |-> k^sharp, is linear and is the inverse of iota, so (v^flat)^sharp = v for v^flat := iota(v) and (k^sharp)^flat = k for every k; in particular k^sharp = 0 if and only if k = 0. (d) If (e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) is an eta-orthonormal ordered basis of V (lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis) and k_a := k(e_a) are the components of k in it, then k^sharp = -k_0 e_0 + k_1 e_1 + k_2 e_2 + k_3 e_3; that is, in this basis (k^sharp)^0 = -k_0 and (k^sharp)^i = k_i for i = 1,2,3, and eta(k^sharp,k^sharp) = -(k_0)^2 + (k_1)^2 + (k_2)^2 + (k_3)^2. Hence k^sharp is null exactly when (k_0)^2 = (k_1)^2 + (k_2)^2 + (k_3)^2, timelike when the left side is smaller, and spacelike when it is larger (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors). No orientation, time orientation or affine structure is used, and no choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Proof strategy. (a) Linearity in v is the bilinearity of eta; iota(v) = 0 is the statement that v lies in the left radical, and the defining nondegeneracy clause says the left radical is {0}. (b) The dual basis theorem (thm-dual-family-is-a-basis-in-finite-dimension) exhibits a basis of V* with one element per basis element of V, so dim V* = dim V; an injective linear map between finite-dimensional spaces of equal dimension is bijective, either directly by thm-rank-nullity (nullity 0 forces rank = dim V = dim V*) or by the equivalent characterization of invertibility. (c) Surjectivity supplies existence, injectivity supplies uniqueness, and the two inverse identities are immediate from the definitions. (d) Evaluate eta(-k_0 e_0 + sum_i k_i e_i, e_b) using eta-orthonormality: eta(-k_0 e_0, e_0) = -k_0 eta(e_0,e_0) = -k_0(-1) = k_0 and eta(k_i e_i, e_i) = k_i (no summation), with all cross terms zero; this equals k_b on the basis, hence the covectors agree by linearity, giving the component formula. The quadratic form is the diagonal evaluation diag(-1,1,1,1); the causal trichotomy is the definition of causal character. The statement is pure algebra of the Lorentz form and asserts nothing physical. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Affine phase functions and wave covectors on affine Minkowski space
items.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space (def-sr-affine-minkowski-model), with displacements q - p in V (def-affine-space-and-displacement). (a) A map theta: A -> R is an affine phase function if there are q in A and a covector k in V* (def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional) with theta(p) - theta(q) = k(p - q) for all p in A; the covector k is then unique (the differential d theta of theta, called its wave covector only when k is nonzero), and for each fixed q the map theta |-> (k, theta(q)) is a bijection onto V* x R, with theta(p) = k(p - q) + theta(q). In the inertial chart x of a frame (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) one has theta(p) = k_a x^a(p) + theta(o) with k_a := k(e_a) the components of k in the frame (thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis), and theta(o') = theta(o) + k(o' - o) for two origins. (b) Constant-phase directions: for v in V one has k(v) = 0 if and only if theta is constant on the line p + R v for every p in A, since theta(p + s v) = theta(p) + s k(v); if k is nonzero, the direction subspace ker k := {v in V : k(v) = 0} is a 3-dimensional linear subspace and every nonempty level set Sigma_t := {p in A : theta(p) = t} is the affine hyperplane p_0 + ker k through any of its points p_0; if k = 0 then theta is constant and Sigma_t is empty or all of A. For every C^1 curve gamma: I -> A one has (theta o gamma)'(s) = k(gamma'(s)) (thm-chain-rule, def-derivative). (c) A wave covector on (A,V,eta) is a nonzero element k of V*, and with k^sharp the raised vector of lem-sr-metric-duality-on-lorentz-vector-space k is called null, timelike or spacelike when eta(k^sharp,k^sharp) is zero, negative or positive, and future, past, future null, past null or causal when k^sharp is respectively future causal, past causal, future null, past null or causal in the sense of def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets; a future null wave covector is one that is both future and null. These definitions are well posed because the causal classification of a nonzero vector is by the sign of eta and by membership in the closed cones, and k^sharp = 0 exactly when k = 0 (duality lemma). (d) This item introduces mathematical objects and terminology only: it excludes the zero covector from 'wave covector', it fixes no units and no physical interpretation, and no claim that light or any physical wave is described by such a phase is made here; that identification is adopted in post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Proof strategy. (a) Uniqueness of k: if k and k' both satisfy the defining identity then (k - k')(p - q) = 0 for all p, so k - k' = 0; the bijection with V* x R is the two inverse constructions theta |-> (d theta, theta(q)) and (k, theta_0) |-> [p |-> k(p - q) + theta_0]. The chart formula is the affine chart identity x(p) - x(q) = (x^a(p) - x^a(q)) e_a together with linearity of k. (b) The displayed identity theta(p + s v) = theta(p) + s k(v) is linearity of k in the displacement; the kernel of a nonzero linear functional on a 4-dimensional space is 3-dimensional (thm-rank-nullity) and the level set is a coset of it. The curve derivative is the chain rule for theta o gamma, whose total derivative at p is k for every p (the phase is affine). (c) The definitions transfer verbatim the vector classification of def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors and def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets along the linear bijection sharp of lem-sr-metric-duality-on-lorentz-vector-space; injectivity of sharp makes the zero-covector exclusion and the well-definedness statement true. (d) A definition item carries formulation obligations only, so no proof of a physical claim is manufactured. Scope: pure linear algebra and affine geometry on A; no choice principle is used.

items.title: A future timelike vector pairs negatively with every nonzero future causal vector
items.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space, let n, v be in V, and recall that a nonzero v with eta(v,v) <= 0 is causal (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets). Then: (a) if n is future timelike and v is nonzero future causal, then eta(n,v) < 0; (b) if n is future timelike and v is nonzero past causal, then eta(n,v) > 0; (c) consequently, for a nonzero null vector v and any future timelike n, v is future null if and only if eta(n,v) < 0, and v is past null if and only if eta(n,v) > 0; the sign of eta(n,v) does not depend on the choice of the future timelike n; (d) if n_hat := n / sqrt(-eta(n,n)) is the normalization of a future timelike n, then n_hat is future unit timelike (eta(n_hat,n_hat) = -1) and eta(n,v) = sqrt(-eta(n,n)) eta(n_hat,v) for every v, so the sign statements hold for n_hat as well. The statement is pure affine Minkowski geometry and no choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Proof strategy. Choose an inertial frame (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3), which exists by lem-future-oriented-inertial-frames-exist with first vector e_0 in C^+; write x = x^0 e_0 + x_vec, where x_vec := sum_{i=1}^3 x^i e_i belongs to S = span(e_1,e_2,e_3), with delta:S x S -> R the restriction of eta and |x_vec| = sqrt(sum_i (x^i)^2) (def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame). By lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components, the future timelike set is {x : x^0 > |x_vec|}, the closed future cone is {x : x^0 >= |x_vec|}, and the closed past cone is {x : x^0 <= -|x_vec|}. Hence n^0 > |n_vec| >= 0 for future timelike n, and for nonzero future causal v one has v^0 >= |v_vec| and v^0 > 0 (if v^0 = 0 then |v_vec| = 0 and v = 0, excluded). Then eta(n,v) = -n^0 v^0 + delta(n_vec,v_vec) <= -n^0 v^0 + |n_vec||v_vec| by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for delta (thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite), and |v_vec| <= v^0 gives eta(n,v) <= -(n^0 - |n_vec|) v^0 < 0 because n^0 - |n_vec| > 0 and v^0 > 0. This proves (a); (b) applies (a) to -v, which is nonzero future causal exactly when v is nonzero past causal, and eta(n,-v) = -eta(n,v). (c) For a nonzero null v exactly one of 'v future' and 'v past' holds (the closed cones meet only at 0 and every nonzero causal vector is future or past); (a) and (b) then identify the sign cases; the 'for every/some' uniformity is immediate because (a) applies to every future timelike n once v is known to be future. (d) eta(n,n) < 0 makes the square root real and positive, n_hat is future timelike by convexity of the cone and has unit norm, and eta is homogeneous in each argument. Scope note: no physical claim; no choice principle is used.

items.title: Frame data of a future null wave covector: the unique pair (varpi, s) with |s| = 1
items.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space, let k be a future null wave covector (def-sr-affine-phase-and-wave-covector) and let (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) be an inertial frame with inertial chart x. Define varpi := -k(e_0) and s_i := k(e_i)/varpi for i = 1,2,3, and write s := (s_1,s_2,s_3) in R^3 with Euclidean norm |s|. Then: (a) varpi > 0. (b) |s| = 1. (c) for every v = v^0 e_0 + v^1 e_1 + v^2 e_2 + v^3 e_3 in V one has k(v) = varpi(-v^0 + s_1 v^1 + s_2 v^2 + s_3 v^3); equivalently the components of k in the frame are (k_0,k_1,k_2,k_3) = (-varpi, varpi s_1, varpi s_2, varpi s_3). (d) the raised vector is k^sharp = varpi(e_0 + s_1 e_1 + s_2 e_2 + s_3 e_3), with frame coordinates varpi(1,s_1,s_2,s_3); it is nonzero and future null, and k(k^sharp) = eta(k^sharp,k^sharp) = 0. (e) conversely, if a covector k in V* has frame components (-varpi, varpi s_1, varpi s_2, varpi s_3) with varpi > 0 and |s| = 1 in some inertial frame, then k is a future null wave covector and the construction of (a)-(b) applied to k in that frame returns the same varpi and s. (f) the pair (varpi,s) is uniquely determined by k and the frame; it is the complete frame description of a future null wave covector. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Proof strategy. (a) k(e_0) = eta(k^sharp,e_0) by the defining property of k^sharp (lem-sr-metric-duality-on-lorentz-vector-space), and eta(k^sharp,e_0) < 0 by lem-sr-future-causal-pairing-negative applied to the future timelike vector e_0 and the nonzero future null vector k^sharp; hence varpi = -k(e_0) > 0. (b) By lem-sr-metric-duality-on-lorentz-vector-space(d), the nullness eta(k^sharp,k^sharp) = 0 reads -(k_0)^2 + (k_1)^2 + (k_2)^2 + (k_3)^2 = 0; with k_0 = -varpi and k_i = k(e_i) = varpi s_i this is varpi^2(-1 + |s|^2) = 0, and varpi > 0 gives |s| = 1. (c) is linearity of k along the unique basis expansion (thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis). (d) The component formula of the duality lemma gives k^sharp = -k_0 e_0 + sum_i k_i e_i = varpi e_0 + varpi sum_i s_i e_i; evaluating eta(k^sharp,k^sharp) with the diagonal matrix and using (b) gives 0, and k^sharp = varpi(1,s) in the frame has positive time component varpi > 0 equal to the norm of its spatial part, which is future null by lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components. (e) With the displayed components the duality lemma gives the vector varpi(1,s), which is nonzero future null by the same closed-cone description, and applying (a)-(b) to it returns varpi and s by construction. (f) Uniqueness is immediate because the components k_a = k(e_a) are determined by k and the frame and (a)-(c) invert them. Scope: pure algebra of eta in one inertial frame; no physical interpretation and no choice principle.

items.title: Transformation of the frame data of a future null wave covector under a passive boost
items.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space, let x and x' be inertial charts whose transition is x' = B(beta) x + b for some beta in R^3 with |beta| < 1 and some b in R^4, where B(beta) is the passive boost of def-lorentz-boost and gamma := (1 - |beta|^2)^(-1/2), and let k be a future null wave covector with frame-x data (varpi,s) as in lem-sr-null-covector-frame-data, so that k has components (k_0,k_1,k_2,k_3) = (-varpi, varpi s_1, varpi s_2, varpi s_3) in x. Then: (i) the components of the same covector k in x' are k'_a = (B(-beta))^b_a k_b, that is k'_0 = gamma(k_0 + beta . k_vec) and k'_vec = k_vec + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . k_vec) beta + gamma beta k_0 for beta nonzero (and k' = k for beta = 0), where k_vec := (k_1,k_2,k_3). (ii) With varpi' := -k'_0 and s'_i := k'_i/varpi' the frame-x' data is varpi' = gamma(1 - beta . s) varpi > 0 and s' = [s + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . s) beta - gamma beta] / [gamma(1 - beta . s)] for beta nonzero (and s' = s for beta = 0); moreover |s'| = 1, so k'_a = (-varpi', varpi' s'_1, varpi' s'_2, varpi' s'_3) in x'. (iii) In the axis case beta = b e_1 with b in (-1,1): s'_1 = (s_1 - b)/(1 - b s_1), s'_2 = s_2/(gamma(1 - b s_1)) and s'_3 = s_3/(gamma(1 - b s_1)). (iv) beta . s' = (beta . s - |beta|^2)/(1 - beta . s); in particular beta . s' = 0 if and only if beta . s = |beta|^2, and beta . s' = -|beta|^2 if and only if beta . s = 0. (v) applying the transformation with beta replaced by -beta returns the original data (varpi,s), since B(-beta) is the inverse of B(beta). The statement is pure algebra of eta and the boost; no choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Proof strategy. (i) The transition x' = B(beta)x + b has linear part Lambda = B(beta), which is a proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix representing the inertial frame change (lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz, def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group); the covector component law k'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a k_b is clause (ii) of thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation (for the constant covector field k, of class C^infinity in the sense of def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space). By lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse, Lambda^{-1} has entries (B(-beta))^0_0 = gamma, (B(-beta))^0_i = (B(-beta))^i_0 = gamma beta_i and (B(-beta))^i_j = delta^i_j + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2) beta_i beta_j (for beta nonzero), which gives the displayed component formulas. (ii) Insert k_0 = -varpi and k_i = varpi s_i: k'_0 = gamma(-varpi + varpi beta . s) = -gamma(1 - beta . s) varpi, so varpi' = gamma(1 - beta . s) varpi; positivity follows from |beta| < 1 and |s| = 1 via the Cauchy-Schwarz bound beta . s <= |beta| < 1 (thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite), so 1 - beta . s >= 1 - |beta| > 0. The numerator for k'_vec is k_vec + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . k_vec) beta + gamma beta k_0 = varpi[s + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . s) beta - gamma beta], so dividing by varpi' gives the displayed s'. Finally |s'| = 1 is not assumed but follows from part (b) of lem-sr-null-covector-frame-data applied in the inertial frame x': the same covector k is future null (k^sharp is unchanged by a change of frame; only its components change), and the lemma's construction in x' returns precisely (varpi', s') as computed. (iii) Substituting beta = b e_1 and |beta|^2 = b^2 gives s'_1 = (s_1 - b)/(1 - b s_1) and s'_j = s_j/(gamma(1 - b s_1)) for j = 2,3. (iv) beta . s' = [beta . s + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . s)|beta|^2 - gamma|beta|^2]/[gamma(1 - beta . s)] = [gamma(beta . s) - gamma|beta|^2]/[gamma(1 - beta . s)] = (beta . s - |beta|^2)/(1 - beta . s); the two equivalences follow since |beta| < 1. (v) By lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse B(-beta) is the inverse of B(beta), so applying the component law twice returns k'' = k; equivalently substituting -beta in (ii) inverts the explicit formulas. Scope note: pure algebra; the item asserts no physical Doppler statement (that is pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration) and no choice principle is used.

items.title: The phase rate along a curve, a worldline and an ideal observer
items.statement: Let theta be an affine phase function with wave covector k (def-sr-affine-phase-and-wave-covector). (a) For every C^1 curve gamma: I -> A one has (theta o gamma)'(s) = k(gamma'(s)) for all s in I. (b) If x: I -> A is a future timelike worldline (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline) with proper-time function tau (def-sr-proper-time) and four-velocity U = dx/dtau (def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration), then d(theta o x)/dtau = k(U) along the worldline (the derivative is taken in the proper-time parametrization; the inverse proper-time parametrization exists by lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization). (c) If k is moreover a future null wave covector, then k(U) < 0 at every point, so theta is strictly decreasing in proper time along every future timelike worldline; the positive number -k(U) is the quantity given physical meaning in def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency. (d) If x is the straight worldline of an inertial observer, so that U = c n for a future unit timelike vector n with eta(n,n) = -1, then k(U) = c k(n) and -k(U) = -c k(n) > 0; conversely every future timelike worldline has eta(U,U) = -c^2 (thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition(a)). No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Proof strategy. (a) In an inertial chart theta is the affine function x |-> k_a x^a + theta_0; composing with gamma and differentiating is the chain rule (thm-chain-rule, def-derivative), and the derivative of the affine part is the constant covector k applied to gamma'. (b) Write the worldline in proper-time parametrization, x = x(tau); then theta o x has derivative k(x'(tau)) = k(U(tau)) by (a) applied to the reparametrized curve, with the chain rule and the positivity of dtau/ds (lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization). (c) U is nonzero future timelike and k^sharp is nonzero future null, so eta(k^sharp,U) < 0 by lem-sr-future-causal-pairing-negative; by the defining property of k^sharp, k(U) = eta(k^sharp,U) < 0. (d) For an inertial observer, thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition(a),(d) gives eta(U,U) = -c^2 and the unit vector n = U/c; linearity gives k(U) = c k(n), and positivity is (c). Scope note: the item is conditional geometry along worldlines; it asserts no clock reading and no frequency measurement, and no choice principle is used.

items.title: Null wave covectors, frame frequency data and the observer frequency of an ideal plane wave
items.statement: Adopt the SI coordinate and unit conventions of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions: in every inertial chart x^0 = c t with c > 0 in metres per second and spatial coordinates in metres, so c is the model's conversion constant. Let k be a future null wave covector and theta its affine phase (def-sr-affine-phase-and-wave-covector). (a) Frame data as wave data. In the inertial chart of a frame let (varpi,s) be the frame data of lem-sr-null-covector-frame-data, so varpi = -k(e_0) > 0 and |s| = 1. Define the angular frequency omega := c varpi (unit s^-1), the linear frequency nu := omega/(2 pi) (unit s^-1, hertz), the wave vector kappa := (omega/c) s (unit m^-1; |kappa| = omega/c), the wavelength lambda := 2 pi/|kappa| = 2 pi c/omega = c/nu (unit m), and the propagation direction s (dimensionless). In these conventions the phase is theta(p) = -omega t + kappa . x_vec(p) + const with t := x^0(p)/c the coordinate time in seconds, so the components of k in the chart are k_a = (-omega/c, (omega/c)s_1, (omega/c)s_2, (omega/c)s_3). (b) Observer frequency. For an ideal observer whose four-velocity is U_o = c n with n in V future unit timelike (eta(n,n) = -1; def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration, thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition) define the observer angular frequency of the wave as omega_n := -c k(n) = -k(U_o) in s^-1, and the observer linear frequency as omega_n/(2 pi); by lem-sr-phase-rate-along-worldline this is minus the rate of change of the phase with respect to the observer's own proper time, and the sign convention makes it positive. (c) Well-definedness. varpi = -k(e_0) > 0 and |s| = 1 in every inertial frame (frame-data lemma), hence omega > 0 and lambda > 0 are well defined and independent of the choices made in their computation; omega_n > 0 for every future unit timelike n and every future null wave covector (lem-sr-future-causal-pairing-negative), so every ideal observer reads a positive angular frequency; omega_n depends only on k and the observer vector n. (d) This item fixes definitions, units and sign conventions only. It does not assert that any physical light is described by such a phase; that identification is adopted in post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model. It contains no quantum identification of energy with hbar omega, no amplitude or intensity content, no medium or dispersion model, no source or detector model and no measurement or empirical claim.
items.strategy: Formulation obligations, not a proof of a physical claim. (a) The definitions are functions of k and the frame; well-definedness of varpi and s is lem-sr-null-covector-frame-data and the SI conversion is def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions, so the physical names attached to the mathematical numbers are a convention fixed here. The relation theta(p) = -omega t + kappa . x_vec(p) + const is the substitution x^0 = c t in k_a x^a. (b) n = U_o/c is future unit timelike by thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition(a); omega_n = -c k(n) = -k(U_o) by linearity; positivity and the proper-time-derivative reading are lem-sr-future-causal-pairing-negative and lem-sr-phase-rate-along-worldline with the sign convention explicitly chosen here. (c) Positivity and uniqueness in each named frame are supplied by the quoted lemmas. (d) The scope clause records that the physical interpretation (light is described by an ideal plane wave, and the number defined here is the frequency an ideal observer reads) is adopted only in post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model; the definition item must not be presented as implying it. No proof of a physical claim is manufactured; no choice principle is used. Angular well-definedness: define the dot product and norm of spatial coordinate triples by their three-entry sums; thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite gives |v dot w| <= |v||w|, so nonzero v,w have positive norms and normalized dot product in [-1,1], the domain of the constructed arccos.

items.title: Adopted ideal plane-wave and frequency-reading model
items.statement: Adopt as physical assumptions of this framework, extending post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light (ideal vacuum light rays are exactly the future null straight lines, with coordinate speed c in every inertial chart) and post-sr-inertial-covariance (the affine Minkowski model, with the model's equations covariant under proper orthochronous affine Lorentz maps): (i) Ideal plane wave. An ideal monochromatic light wave in vacuum is modeled, in any inertial chart, by a dimensionless affine phase theta with future null wave covector k (def-sr-affine-phase-and-wave-covector, lem-sr-null-covector-frame-data): the level sets of theta are the wave fronts, every line p + R k^sharp has constant phase, and the rays of this ideal wave are the future null straight lines p + R_{>=0} k^sharp, consistently with the general ideal-light clause that the ideal vacuum light rays are exactly the future null straight lines. The model is one ideal plane wave: constant wave covector, no medium, no dispersion, no absorption, no modulation or envelope, no boundary or source model, no intensity or polarization model. (ii) Frequency reading. An ideal observer of the model with four-velocity U_o = c n (n future unit timelike) that receives this wave reads the angular frequency omega_n := -c k(n) = -k(U_o) and the linear frequency omega_n/(2 pi) of def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency, i.e. minus the rate of change of the phase with respect to the observer's own proper time with the sign convention that this number is positive (lem-sr-phase-rate-along-worldline, lem-sr-future-causal-pairing-negative). The reading is attached to the observer's worldline at the event of reception. (iii) Frequency comparisons. Comparing the frequency of one wave between two ideal observers or between two inertial descriptions means comparing omega_n at specified reception events, or the frame data (omega,s) of the same phase function in specified inertial charts; this postulate asserts no Doppler or aberration formula, and comparing events requires propagating the phase along the specified observer worldlines. (iv) Scope and exclusions. These are adopted idealizations, not deductions from experiment and not claims about nature. No quantum photon model and no identification of energy with hbar omega is made (excluded by the conventions of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions); no claim is made that real light, real clocks, real receivers or real sources are exactly described; dispersive, absorbing, nonlinear or modulated media, finite line width, intensity, polarization, source and detector physics, gravitation, quantum effects and accelerated-observer reception are outside the model. Empirical tests of the model belong to the framework's experimental work and are not asserted here.
items.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem: it fixes the physical interpretation of the mathematical phase functions and of the observer-frequency number, and it fixes the ideal wave and receiver regime. Obligations: (i) the phase functions with future null wave covectors and their level sets are mathematical objects supplied by def-sr-affine-phase-and-wave-covector and lem-sr-null-covector-frame-data; the identification of the level sets with wave fronts and of the future null lines along k^sharp with this wave's rays is adopted, extending the ideal-light clause of post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light; for a single plane wave every future null straight line of constant phase is exactly a line p + R_{>=0} k^sharp, so the adoption introduces no competing ray system. (ii) The reading rule is an identification of a physical clock reading of a periodic process with the mathematical number -k(U_o); the mathematical positivity and the proper-time derivative are lem-sr-phase-rate-along-worldline and lem-sr-future-causal-pairing-negative, while the identification itself is adopted. (iii) The postulate is deliberately silent about Doppler and aberration formulas, so it cannot be used to infer them; the comparison protocol is fixed so that downstream theorems state exactly which frequencies at which events they compare. (iv) The exclusions are part of the adopted content and must travel with every conclusion. No proof is manufactured; no choice principle is used.

items.title: Doppler shift and aberration for an ideal plane wave between inertial descriptions
items.statement: Adopt post-sr-inertial-covariance, post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light and post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model, and the conventions of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions. Let x and x' be inertial charts whose transition is x' = B(beta) x + b with beta in R^3, |beta| < 1, b in R^4 and B(beta) the passive boost of def-lorentz-boost; write gamma := (1 - |beta|^2)^(-1/2) and beta_hat := beta/|beta| for beta nonzero, so that the frame x' moves with velocity v = c beta relative to the frame x in the direction beta_hat. Let the ideal wave of the model have phase theta with future null wave covector k and frame-x data (omega,s) in the sense of def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency: omega > 0, s in R^3 with |s| = 1 and k_a = (-omega/c, (omega/c)s) in x. Then, conditionally on the adopted model: (i) Frame data in x'. The data of the same covector k in x' is (omega',s') with omega' = gamma(1 - beta . s) omega > 0 and s' = [s + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . s) beta - gamma beta]/[gamma(1 - beta . s)] for beta nonzero (and omega' = omega, s' = s for beta = 0), so |s'| = 1 and k'_a = (-omega'/c, (omega'/c)s'_1, (omega'/c)s'_2, (omega'/c)s'_3) in x'. In the axis case beta = b e_1 with b in (-1,1): s'_1 = (s_1 - b)/(1 - b s_1) and (s'_2,s'_3) = (s_2,s_3)/(gamma(1 - b s_1)). (ii) Reading and frequency ratios. The rest observers of x and x' (four-velocities c e_0 and c e'_0) read angular frequencies omega = -c k(e_0) and omega' = -c k(e'_0); the linear frequencies and wavelengths of the two descriptions satisfy nu' = gamma(1 - beta . s) nu and lambda' = lambda/[gamma(1 - beta . s)]. More generally, an ideal observer whose coordinate velocity in x is w (a vector of the frame's spatial three-space with |w| < c) reads omega_o = gamma_w(1 - (w . s)/c) omega, where gamma_w := (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^(-1/2); equivalently omega_o = gamma_w(1 - beta_w . s) omega with beta_w := w/c. (iii) Longitudinal cases. If s = beta_hat then omega' = omega sqrt((1 - |beta|)/(1 + |beta|)) < omega, nu' = nu sqrt((1 - |beta|)/(1 + |beta|)) and lambda' = lambda sqrt((1 + |beta|)/(1 - |beta|)): the observer moving in the direction of propagation (away from a source at rest in x and located behind it) reads a red-shifted frequency and lengthened wavelength. If s = -beta_hat then omega' = omega sqrt((1 + |beta|)/(1 - |beta|)) > omega and lambda' = lambda sqrt((1 - |beta|)/(1 + |beta|)): blue shift for an observer moving opposite to the propagation direction (toward such a source). (iv) Transverse protocols. If beta . s = 0 (propagation direction perpendicular to the relative velocity in the frame x) then omega' = gamma omega; this is greater than omega when beta!=0 and equals omega when beta=0. If beta . s = |beta|^2, for beta!=0 equivalently s' . beta_hat = 0 (propagation direction perpendicular to the relative velocity in the frame x'), then omega' = omega/gamma; this is less than omega when beta!=0 and equals omega when beta=0. Both configurations are called transverse Doppler configurations in the literature and the two factors differ for beta!=0 (both equal one at beta=0); the direction and size of the shift are not determined by the word 'transverse' without specifying the frame in which transversality holds. (v) Aberration. For beta!=0, if theta_x, theta_x' in [0,pi] are the angles between the propagation directions s, s' and the boost axis beta_hat, then cos theta_x' = (cos theta_x - |beta|)/(1 - |beta| cos theta_x); the map u |-> (u - |beta|)/(1 - |beta| u) is a strictly increasing bijection of [-1,1] onto itself, and in particular cos theta_x = 0 gives cos theta_x' = -|beta|. (vi) Scope and protocol. All clauses concern one ideal plane wave and ideal observers, and frequencies are compared through the phase model at specified reception events; the results are conditional on the adopted postulates (ideal plane wave, ideal clocks, inertial covariance, flat classical spacetime) and are not empirical claims about nature, sources or apparatus. They exclude media and dispersion, modulation and signal speeds, intensity and polarization, real line widths, accelerating observers (reserved to the framework's accelerated-observer page), gravitation and quantum effects; no statistical or measurement statement is made. If beta = 0 the transition is the pure translation x'=x+b: the inertial axes and wave-covector frame data agree, with omega'=omega and s'=s, while the affine phase constant is transformed as in the covector/phase law.
items.strategy: Proof in dependency order; the mathematical core is lem-sr-null-covector-boost-transformation with the reading lemmas. (i) By def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency the frame data of k in x is (omega,s) with omega = c varpi, varpi = -k(e_0), and k_a = (-omega/c,(omega/c)s). Apply lem-sr-null-covector-boost-transformation(i)-(ii) with (varpi,s): its conclusions give varpi' = gamma(1 - beta . s) varpi > 0 and the displayed s' with |s'| = 1; multiplying by c gives omega' = gamma(1 - beta . s) omega; the axis formulas are clause (iii) of the lemma. The relation beta . s = |beta|^2 <=> s' . beta_hat = 0 is clause (iv) of the lemma, and the identity s' . beta_hat = (beta . s - |beta|^2)/(|beta|(1 - beta . s)) for beta nonzero is its display. (ii) For the rest observer of x, U = c e_0 and omega = -c k(e_0) by the definition; for x' likewise with the frame vector e'_0 (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart). The wavelength ratio is the reciprocal of the frequency ratio because lambda = c/nu and lambda' = c/nu' by definition. For a general observer write U_o = gamma_w(c,w) by thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition(e); then k(U_o) = c gamma_w k(e_0) + gamma_w k(w), and k(w) = (omega/c) w . s because w lies in the frame's spatial three-space and k_a = (-omega/c,(omega/c)s) (def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame); hence omega_o = -k(U_o) = gamma_w(omega - (omega/c) w . s) = gamma_w(1 - (w . s)/c) omega. (iii) Substitute s = +/- beta_hat into (i): gamma(1 -/+ |beta|) = sqrt((1 -/+ |beta|)/(1 +/- |beta|)) because gamma^2(1 -/+ |beta|)^2 = (1 -/+ |beta|)/(1 +/- |beta|); the wavelength ratios are the reciprocals. The receding/approaching identification uses the fixed protocol: the source is at rest in x and the wave propagates from it, so s = beta_hat means the x'-rest observer moves away from the source and s = -beta_hat means it moves toward it. (iv) beta . s = 0 gives omega' = gamma omega from (i); beta . s = |beta|^2 gives omega' = gamma(1 - |beta|^2) omega = omega/gamma, and the equivalence with s' . beta_hat = 0 is the displayed identity; at beta=0 both read omega'=omega and no direction beta_hat is assigned; for nonzero beta, gamma>1 gives the stated strict inequalities. The two protocols are distinct because a unit s with beta . s = 0 is not a unit s with beta . s = |beta|^2 when |beta| > 0. The existence of both configurations for every |beta| < 1 is exhibited by the examples on the companion page. (v) For beta!=0 set b:=|beta| and use the invariant display s' . beta_hat = (beta . s - b^2)/(b(1 - beta . s)). Substitute beta . s=b cos theta_x and cancel the strictly positive b to obtain cos theta_x'=(cos theta_x-b)/(1-b cos theta_x). No division of a coordinate axis formula by beta is used. The denominator is positive on [-1,1] because 0<b<1, and the derivative of u |-> (u-b)/(1-bu) is (1-b^2)/(1-bu)^2>0; its endpoint values are -1 and1, so it is the stated strictly increasing bijection. At beta=0 frequency/direction data agree and no boost-axis angle is assigned. (vi) The scope clause records the hypotheses and the exclusions; no step uses a source or detector model, and no choice principle is used. The postulate post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model supplies the physical interpretation of theta, k and the reading rule, and the two other postulates supply the model's light and covariance clauses; the deduction is conditional on all of them.

items.title: Units, coordinate conventions and c restoration for the wave and Doppler formulas
items.statement: Remark on the conventions of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions and def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency, for use with pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration. (a) Units in the adopted coordinates x^0 = c t: the phase theta is dimensionless; the coordinates x^a, the wavelength lambda and all distances are in metres; the components k_a of a wave covector, the wave vector kappa and varpi = -k(e_0) are in m^-1; the angular frequencies omega and omega_n and the linear frequencies nu are in s^-1 (nu also in hertz); c is in m s^-1; and s, beta, beta_w and gamma are dimensionless. (b) Two coordinate forms. In the adopted coordinates theta = -omega t + kappa . x_vec + const and k_a = (-omega/c, (omega/c)s); in a chart whose time coordinate is t in seconds directly, so that the metric component g_tt = -c^2 carries m^2 s^-2 and the time-space components carry m s^-1, the same phase is theta = -omega t + kappa . x_vec + const with the same omega and kappa, and the component tuple (-omega, (omega/c)s) carries mixed units; formulas derived in one convention are not reused unchanged in the other. This is the general warning of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions specialized to the wave covector. (c) Natural units and restoration. In natural units c = 1 with x^0 = t one has k_a = (-omega, omega s), lambda = 2 pi/omega, and the Doppler and aberration factors gamma(1 - beta . s) and sqrt((1 -/+ |beta|)/(1 +/- |beta|)) are unchanged; restoring dimensions means replacing k_0 by -omega/c, k_i by (omega/c)s_i, writing every velocity as v = c beta with the dimensionless beta, and replacing lambda by 2 pi c/omega = c/nu. The dimensionless factors gamma(1 - beta . s) and the longitudinal square roots need no c restoration because they contain only beta, s and gamma; the c restoration affects the map between omega, nu, lambda and the components of k, not the shift factors themselves. (d) This remark introduces no quantum identification of energy with hbar omega, no amplitude or intensity content and no measurement claim; it is a units and convention statement carrying the scope of the items it cites.
items.strategy: A conventions and units remark, not a theorem. (a) Each unit is read off from the definitions in def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions and def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency: the phase is dimensionless by (theta(p) = k(p - q) + theta_0 with k in m^-1 and displacements in m), and the wave quantities inherit their units from k, c and the definitions omega = c varpi, kappa = (omega/c)s, lambda = c/nu. (b) Substituting x^0 = c t into k_a x^a gives -omega t + kappa . x_vec; the metric-component statement is the convention clause of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions for a chart with time coordinate in seconds, and the mixed-unit tuple is displayed to prevent copying formulas across conventions. (c) The natural-unit form is the substitution c = 1 in the same formulas (with x^0 = t), and the restoration list is the inverse substitution; the factors gamma(1 - beta . s) and sqrt((1 -/+ |beta|)/(1 +/- |beta|)) are functions of the dimensionless quantities beta, s, gamma alone, which is why they are invariant under the restoration. (d) The exclusions repeat the scope of the cited items; no step proves a physical claim and no choice principle is used.

items.title: Worked longitudinal Doppler shift at beta = 3/5
items.statement: Worked example in the model of sr-light-and-doppler. Let x and x' be inertial charts with x' = B(beta) x + b, beta = (3/5) e_1, so gamma = 5/4 and the frame x' moves with velocity (3/5)c e_1 relative to x. Let an ideal plane wave have frame-x data (omega,s) with omega > 0 and (a) s = e_1, (b) s = -e_1. Then pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration gives: (a) omega' = gamma(1 - 3/5) omega = (5/4)(2/5) omega = omega/2, nu' = nu/2, lambda' = 2 lambda and s' = e_1; an observer at rest in x' moving in the direction of propagation (away from a source at rest in x and located behind it) reads half the frequency and twice the wavelength. In both cases |s'| = 1 and omega' > 0, in agreement with the general theorem; the verification uses only the exact rational values gamma = 5/4, 1 - 3/5 = 2/5 and 1 + 3/5 = 8/5. items.title: Worked transverse Doppler configurations: gamma versus 1/gamma at beta = 3/5
items.statement: Worked example in the model of sr-light-and-doppler showing that the transverse Doppler shift depends on the frame in which transversality is required. Let x and x' be inertial charts with x' = B(beta) x + b, beta = (3/5) e_1 and gamma = 5/4, and let an ideal plane wave have frame-x data (omega,s) with omega > 0. (a) If s = e_2, so beta . s = 0 and the propagation direction is perpendicular to the relative velocity in x, then pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration gives omega' = gamma omega = (5/4)omega > omega and s' = (-3/5, 4/5, 0), which has |s'| = 1; the frequency read by the x'-rest observer is blue-shifted by the factor 5/4. (b) If s = (3/5, 4/5, 0), so beta . s = 9/25 = |beta|^2 and equivalently s' . e_1 = 0, the propagation direction is perpendicular to the relative velocity in x', and the theorem gives omega' = gamma(1 - 9/25) omega = (5/4)(16/25) omega = (4/5)omega = omega/gamma < omega and s' = e_2; the frequency read by the x'-rest observer is red-shifted by the factor 4/5. In neither case is omega' = omega for beta nonzero, and the two exact factors differ; a statement of a transverse Doppler shift is therefore incomplete until the frame in which the direction is transverse is specified. Scope: a conditional computation in the ideal plane-wave model; no measurement and no empirical claim.
items.strategy: Verification by substitution into pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration with exact rational arithmetic. (a) With s_1 = 0, s_2 = 1 the axis formulas give s'_1 = (0 - 3/5)/(1 - 0) = -3/5 and s'_2 = s_2/(gamma(1 - 0)) = 1/(5/4) = 4/5, so s' = (-3/5, 4/5, 0), and the frequency factor is gamma(1 - beta . s) = gamma = 5/4. (b) With s_1 = 3/5, s_2 = 4/5 the formulas give s'_1 = (3/5 - 3/5)/(1 - 9/25) = 0 and s'_2 = (4/5)/((5/4)(16/25)) = (4/5)/(4/5) = 1, so s' = e_2, and the frequency factor is gamma(1 - 9/25) = (5/4)(16/25) = 4/5 = 1/gamma. Both cases satisfy |s'| = 1; the identification of the second condition with transversality in x' is s' . e_1 = 0, which the theorem proves equivalent to beta . s = |beta|^2. The example inherits the theorem's scope and exclusions. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Worked aberration and Doppler shift at beta = 3/5 and cos theta = 4/5
items.statement: Worked example in the model of sr-light-and-doppler. Let x and x' be inertial charts with x' = B(beta) x + b, beta = (3/5) e_1 and gamma = 5/4, and let an ideal plane wave have frame-x propagation direction s = (4/5, 3/5, 0), so cos theta = 4/5 and sin theta = 3/5 with theta in [0,pi] the angle between s and the boost axis. Then pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration gives s' = (5/13, 12/13, 0), hence cos theta' = 5/13, and the angular frequency ratio omega'/omega = gamma(1 - beta s_1) = (5/4)(1 - 12/25) = (5/4)(13/25) = 13/20, so nu' = (13/20) nu and lambda' = (20/13) lambda. Since arccos(5/13) > arccos(4/5), the apparent direction of the source, which is opposite to the propagation direction, moves from an angle arccos(-4/5) to an angle arccos(-5/13) measured from the boost axis, i.e. toward the direction of motion of the observer's frame: this is the sign of stellar aberration in this configuration. The example records the exact angle transformation and leaves any observational interpretation to the framework's experimental work. Scope: a conditional computation in the ideal plane-wave model; no measurement and no empirical claim.
items.strategy: Verification by substitution into the theorem with exact rational arithmetic. (a) s'_1 = (4/5 - 3/5)/(1 - (3/5)(4/5)) = (1/5)/(13/25) = 5/13 and s'_2 = (3/5)/((5/4)(13/25)) = (3/5)/(13/20) = 12/13, so s' = (5/13, 12/13, 0) and |s'|^2 = 25/169 + 144/169 = 1. (b) The frequency factor is gamma(1 - beta s_1) = (5/4)(1 - 12/25) = (5/4)(13/25) = 13/20; nu' = (13/20) nu is clause (ii) of the theorem and lambda' = (20/13) lambda is the reciprocal. (c) The angle statement uses cos theta' = s'_1 (axis component) and the strictly increasing map of the theorem's clause (v); the apparent direction is -s' because the wave propagates from the source toward the observer, so its angle to the boost axis is arccos(-s'_1) = arccos(-5/13) and the displacement toward the direction of motion is the standard aberration sign; the example states it as an interpretation of the exact transformation and makes no observational claim. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Worked geometry of the phase level sets of a future null wave covector
items.statement: Worked example for def-sr-affine-phase-and-wave-covector and lem-sr-null-covector-frame-data. Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space, let k be a future null wave covector with frame data (varpi,s) in an inertial frame, so varpi > 0, |s| = 1 and k has components k_a = (-varpi, varpi s_1, varpi s_2, varpi s_3), and let theta be the affine phase with wave covector k. Then: (a) k(k^sharp) = eta(k^sharp,k^sharp) = 0, since the raised vector is k^sharp = varpi(e_0 + s_1 e_1 + s_2 e_2 + s_3 e_3), so theta is constant on every line p + R k^sharp. (b) The direction subspace ker k = {v : k(v) = 0} = {v : v^0 = s . v_vec} is 3-dimensional; for v in ker k one has eta(v,v) = |v_vec|^2 - (s . v_vec)^2 >= 0 by the finite Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, with equality exactly when v_vec is a real multiple of s, i.e. exactly when v lies in the line span(k^sharp); hence the restriction of eta to ker k is positive semidefinite with radical the line span(k^sharp), and the only null direction contained in ker k is the line through k^sharp (with future ray k^sharp and past ray -k^sharp). (c) Every nonempty level set Sigma = {p : theta(p) = theta(p_0)} is the affine hyperplane p_0 + ker k through p_0, whose normal covector is the null covector k; it contains the two null rays p_0 + R_{\ge 0} k^sharp and p_0 + R_{\le 0} k^sharp, and all its other direction vectors are spacelike. The verification is exact algebra; no choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Verification by explicit computation. (a) k^sharp = varpi(1,s) by lem-sr-null-covector-frame-data(d); then k(k^sharp) = -varpi^2 + varpi^2|s|^2 = 0 because |s| = 1, and homogeneity gives theta(p + lambda k^sharp) = theta(p) + lambda k(k^sharp) = theta(p) by the displayed identity of def-sr-affine-phase-and-wave-covector(b). (b) The kernel of the nonzero functional k is 3-dimensional; substituting v^0 = s . v_vec into eta gives eta(v,v) = -(s . v_vec)^2 + |v_vec|^2, and the finite Cauchy-Schwarz inequality (thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite) gives |s . v_vec| <= |s||v_vec| = |v_vec| with equality exactly when v_vec lies in the span of s; for such v one has v = (v^0, v_vec) = (lambda, lambda s) = lambda(1,s) in span(k^sharp), and for all other nonzero v in ker k the form is strictly positive, i.e. spacelike. (c) The level set is a coset of ker k by def-sr-affine-phase-and-wave-covector(b), its normal covector is k (the level sets are exactly the affine hyperplanes with direction ker k), and the null directions in it are those of (b); membership of the two rays follows from (a). The sign of the normal covector's null character is the definition of a null wave covector; no physical interpretation of the level sets is used in the verification. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Counterexample: a transverse wave configuration need not have zero Doppler shift
items.statement: Statement refuted: 'if the propagation direction of an ideal plane wave is perpendicular to the relative velocity of two inertial frames, then the frequency read by the observer at rest in one frame equals the frequency read by the observer at rest in the other, omega' = omega.' Counterexample in the model of sr-light-and-doppler: let x and x' be inertial charts with x' = B(beta) x + b and beta = (3/5) e_1. (a) For the wave with frame-x data s = e_2 one has beta . s = 0, so the propagation direction is perpendicular to the relative velocity in x, and pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration gives omega' = gamma omega = (5/4)omega, which is not omega. (b) For the wave with frame-x data s = (3/5, 4/5, 0) one has s' = e_2, so the propagation direction is perpendicular to the relative velocity in x', and the same theorem gives omega' = (4/5)omega, which is not omega. Hence transversality of the propagation direction to the relative velocity in one of the two frames is compatible with the blue-shifted factor 5/4 and with the red-shifted factor 4/5, and it never gives omega' = omega when beta is nonzero; the refuted statement is false as a universal claim in the ideal model. The counterexample is conditional on the model's ideal plane-wave and ideal-clock assumptions, performs no measurement, and claims no empirical falsification.
items.strategy: Refutation by two exact configurations. (a) Substituting s = e_2 into pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration(i) gives the frequency factor gamma(1 - beta . s) = gamma = 5/4, so omega' = (5/4)omega != omega. (b) Substituting s = (3/5,4/5,0) gives beta . s = 9/25 = |beta|^2, hence the frequency factor gamma(1 - |beta|^2) = 4/5, so omega' = (4/5)omega != omega; the theorem's clause (iv) identifies this case with s'.e_1 = 0, i.e. transversality in x'. Since a single configuration with beta nonzero and omega' != omega refutes the universal claim, and both configurations are within the model's hypotheses, the refutation is complete; the two different factors also show that the shift's direction is protocol-dependent. The counterexample inherits the theorem's scope and excludes all measurement, statistical and empirical claims. No choice principle is used.

(b) Let x' be the inertial chart with x' = B(beta)x + b and beta = (3/5)e_1. The frame-x' data of the same covector is (varpi',s') with varpi'/varpi = gamma(1 - beta . s) = (5/4)(1 - 0) = 5/4 and s' = (-3/5, 12/25, 16/25), since s'_1 = (s_1 - beta)/(1 - beta s_1) = (0 - 3/5)/1 = -3/5, s'_2 = s_2/(gamma(1 - beta s_1)) = (3/5)/(5/4) = 12/25 and s'_3 = s_3/(gamma(1 - beta s_1)) = (4/5)/(5/4) = 16/25; one checks |s'|^2 = 9/25 + 144/625 + 256/625 = 9/25 + 400/625 = 9/25 + 16/25 = 1. (c) Applying the transformation with beta replaced by -beta to (varpi',s') returns (varpi,s): varpi''/varpi' = gamma(1 + (3/5)(-3/5)) = (5/4)(16/25) = 4/5, so varpi'' = (4/5)(5/4)varpi = varpi, and s'' = (0, 3/5, 4/5) by the same axis formulas. The verification is exact rational algebra; no physical interpretation of the data is used and no choice principle is used.
